newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dow seen overcoming 8,000 mark.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dow seen overcoming 8,000 mark.

text.p: U.S. stocks may pause near-term but appear to have enough backing to drive the Dow industrials through the 8,000 mark, technical analysts said on Wednesday.
A continued rally in bonds, coupled with solid trading volume and recent strength in financial stocks are cited as factors giving the market the legs to crack the barrier.

"I expect it to hesitate a bit, see some psychological resistance at 8,000, but I think the ingredients are in place to overcome it short term," said Gregory Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities Inc.
Nie said his data indicated that stock valuations had not yet hit levels that would indicate a near-term pullback.

"I'm willing to speculate two to three more decent days for this phase are possible before we hit the overbought hurdle," he said. "That ought to be enough to get us comfortably above the 8,000 level."
On Wednesday afternoon the Dow was off about 66 at 7895.

A key factor boosting stocks has been the bond market. JW Charles technical analyst Gary Kaltbaum noted in a report that the 30-year bond has broken above important resistance, indicating the yield could fall to 6.4 percent.
The long bond was up 9/32 on Wednesday, its yield dropping to 6.56 percent from 6.58 percent Tuesday.

The strength in bonds has also translated into a rally in financial stocks, which are traditionally sensitive to interest rates. "It's not often that the stock market gets in trouble when financial stocks are acting well," Kaltbaum said.
Elaine Yager, manager technical analysis at Herzog, Heine, Geduld, said she had an upside target for the Dow at 8282.
She cautioned that investors should be prepared for a five percent decline "at any given time," which from 8000 would pull the Dow back to the critical support level of 7600.
Nevertheless, she said she could not find evidence in her charts to indicate major trouble ahead of U.S. stocks.
"My charts say that the trend is up," she said. "It may be difficult to look up that high. It might be a little bit scary for some. But I can't put in something that just isn't there."

After hitting its low for the year on April 11 at 6391.69, the Dow rose almost 25 percent to its record high set Tuesday at 7962.31. The steep climb has some analysts warning that a major decline might very well be around the corner.
"It's been a wonderful bull market," said John Wosczyna, market strategist at Roney & Co. "I think it's an opportunity to take your chips off the table and walk away with the cash."
He said he thought stocks have reached their highs for the year and could be setting up for a decline of up to 30 percent. That would bring the Dow to 5500.
